euronews.description: With a career spanning five decades, the English actress has moved between cult films and "blockbusters". The award she will receive with director Werner Herzog adds to her Oscar, BAFTA, Emmy and Golden Globe nominations.

euronews.description: The government's initial aim is to grow the programme to 10,000 volunteers a year, with a long-term goal of up to 50,000 per year in 2035.

euronews.description: Heads of 21 global and rising powers gather in Bishkek for the SCO summit as wars strain the global order. China and Russia have previously used the SCO to project their influence and their stand against the West, but the middle powers are now there to seek new economic and political momentum.

euronews.description: Hungarian PM Péter Magyar told the Bled Strategic Forum that the EU faces a leadership crisis and must make crucial decisions on its future. He also criticised Brussels' daily migration fines against Hungary, calling them unfair despite a 2020 EU court ruling.

euronews.title: Algerian president seeks to impose death penalty on arsonists
euronews.description: Algeria declared three days of mourning after wildfires killed 12 people and injured dozens. Authorities said 46 fires remained active, with 54 people hospitalised for burns, including six in critical condition.

euronews.title: Argentina great Lionel Messi announces retirement from international football
euronews.description: The decision comes shortly after the death of his father, Jorge Messi, which prompted the former Barcelona and Paris Saint-Germain player to consider his future.

euronews.description: Officials across NATO’s eastern flank say there is no evidence of an imminent Russian attack, even as they strengthen their defences and warn that Moscow’s campaign of sabotage and provocations against Europe is intensifying.

euronews.description: YouTube's new "exposure-based model" counts a view from the first frame, across shorts, long-form videos, podcasts and livestreams, inflating creators' headline numbers without changing how much they actually get paid.

euronews.title: Germany and France float plan to bring Kallas under von der Leyen's supervision
euronews.description: Under the German-Franco plan, Kaja Kallas would have a more hands-on role inside the European Commission, with broader responsibilities. But Ursula von der Leyen would retain the final say on foreign policy.

euronews.title: South African airline Airlink defends dramatic stadium flyover
euronews.description: Footage of the flyover quickly began circulating on social media, prompting mixed reactions as some expressed concerns over safety.

euronews.description: More and more fragments of the Twannberg meteorite are being found in the Bernese Jura. Over 2,200 pieces are now known, and the remains of this rare iron meteorite are highly prized by researchers for several reasons.

lemonde.title: Edouard Balladur, ancien premier ministre, est mort à l’âge de 97 ans
lemonde.description: Secrétaire général de l’Elysée sous Georges Pompidou, négociateur des accords de Grenelle, en 1968, chef du gouvernement sous François Mitterrand en 1993, il avait échoué face à Jacques Chirac lors de la présidentielle de 1995. Personnage incontournable de la Vᵉ République, il s’est éteint lundi 31 août, à 97 ans.

lemonde.title: EN DIRECT, guerre en Ukraine : des frappes mortelles sur Kiev et sa région ; l’Ukraine dit préparer de nouvelles attaques contre la Russie
lemonde.description: Le président ukrainien, Volodymyr Zelensky, a par ailleurs confirmé un échange avec les émissaires du président des Etats-Unis, Donald Trump, Steve Witkoff et Jared Kushner, qui préparent des contacts avec la partie russe ainsi qu’une visite en Ukraine.

lemonde.title: La Cour suprême autorise la poursuite du chantier de la salle de bal à la Maison Blanche
lemonde.description: Le refus de la plus haute juridiction des Etats-Unis de se prononcer sur le fond dans cette affaire et d’envisager la question des prérogatives du Congrès, la renvoyant en première instance, récompense la stratégie du fait accompli, choisie par Donald Trump.

lemonde.title: Apologie du terrorisme : cinq rapporteurs spéciaux de l’ONU prennent la défense de Rima Hassan
lemonde.description: Dans un courrier au gouvernement rendu public lundi, les rapporteurs expriment leurs « vives préoccupations » concernant l’eurodéputée « insoumise » d’origine palestinienne, qui est visée par plusieurs procédures judiciaires.

lemonde.title: Au Népal, après les inondations, les glaciologues sidérés par l’ampleur de la catastrophe
lemonde.description: Les scientifiques de ce pays himalayen connaissent le danger représenté par la fonte accélérée des glaciers. Mais aucun n’avait anticipé un effondrement et une crue de cette magnitude.

lemonde.title: Les bases de données de santé, une mine d’or à exploiter
lemonde.description: Ces éléments  peuvent être utilisés dans le cadre d’études rétrospectives à partir des données observationnelles. Problème, les informations ne sont pas toutes recueillies de façon standardisée.

lemonde.title: Meurtre de Tupac Shakur : Duane Davis reconnu coupable, trente ans après la mort du rappeur
lemonde.description: L’ancien membre de gang, qui a l’intention de faire appel, était poursuivi pour avoir commandité l’attaque contre la légende du rap, tuée à l’âge de 25 ans, et fourni l’arme du crime. Il encourt la perpétuité incompressible.

lemonde.title: New York : une femme tuée à Times Square lors d’une attaque au couteau, l’assaillante abattue par la police
lemonde.description: Selon les autorités qui excluent la piste terroriste, l’assaillante, qui a aussi blessé un homme, était connue pour des troubles psychiatriques. La police lui a tiré dessus alors qu’elle refusait de lâcher ses armes et s’approchait des agents.

lemonde.title: Amazon visé par une plainte pour surfacturation en secret de publicités à plus de 1 million d’annonceurs
lemonde.description: Selon les plaignants, le géant du commerce en ligne aurait surfacturé ses clients annonceurs de plus de 20 milliards de dollars depuis 2019, grâce à un mécanisme d’enchères publicitaires qu’ils jugent trompeur.

lemonde.title: Agression sexuelle sur mineur à Clamart : cinq ans de prison dont un ferme, pour un ancien entraîneur du club de cyclisme
lemonde.description: William Bastit, âgé aujourd’hui de 49 ans, a notamment imposé une fellation à un garçon de 13 ans en 2009, et envoyé plusieurs messages obscènes à une dizaine d’autres.

lemonde.title: L’Union européenne annonce suspendre ses importations de viande brésilienne à partir de jeudi
lemonde.description: Le Brésil avait été retiré en mai d’une liste européenne des pays qui respectent les règles de l’UE qui interdisent l’utilisation abusive d’antibiotiques dans l’élevage.

lemonde.title: La guerre, nouvelle normalité du détroit d’Ormuz
lemonde.description: La reprise des frappes entre les Etats-Unis et l’Iran, lundi, confirme que le conflit s’est installé durablement dans ces eaux. L’outil de dissuasion qu’était pour Téhéran le blocage de cette artère stratégique s’émousse peu à peu.

lemonde.title: Facturation électronique : la réforme entre en vigueur mardi, sans sanction immédiate pour les retardataires
lemonde.description: Promesse de simplification pour les entreprises et nouvel outil de lutte contre la fraude à la TVA pour l’Etat, qui espère un gain de 3 milliards d’euros par an, la réforme concerne 4 millions d’entreprises.

lemonde.title: Le secrétaire à l’armée de terre américain, Dan Driscoll, démissionne après plusieurs mois de tension avec Pete Hegseth
lemonde.description: Ce proche du vice-président, J. D. Vance, a notamment été impliqué dans les négociations concernant la guerre en Ukraine. Aucune raison n’a été donnée pour expliquer son départ mais ses rapports difficiles avec le secrétaire à la défense ont été largement rapportés par la presse.

lemonde.title: Donald Trump multiplie les attaques contre les parcs nationaux américains
lemonde.description: Le gouvernement des Etats-Unis envisage de céder une petite partie du parc de Yosemite, en Californie, à un promoteur privé. Le projet d’attenter à ce lieu mythique suscite un tollé. Il ne s’agit pas la seule initiative visant à rogner les espaces protégés du pays.

lemonde.title: En Guinée, des ONG réclament une enquête indépendante après la découverte de six corps dans une fosse commune
lemonde.description: Les six dépouilles, toutes celles d’hommes, avaient été découvertes dans une forêt de la préfecture de Forécariah, en Basse-Guinée, par des jeunes qui ramassaient du bois de chauffe.

rfi.title: Ten years after Gabon’s post-election violence, painful questions remain
rfi.description: Ten years on, victims of violence that followed president Ali Bongo’s disputed re-election in Gabon are still demanding truth and justice. Questions also remain over the possible involvement of French nationals and the response of the French authorities.

rfi.title: Niger coup attempt: 'Russians saved the day' analyst tells RFI
rfi.description: Niger’s military government has survived its most serious internal challenge since seizing power in 2023, after Russian paramilitaries helped loyalist forces crush last Saturday's attempted coup in the capital, Niamey. RFI spoke to an expert who explains how this episode has left General Abdourahamane Tiani’s junta weakened and more dependent on Russia.

rfi.title: France's international photojournalism festival founder Leroy dies aged 69
rfi.description: Tributes have been pouring in for Jean-François Leroy, the founder of the Visa pour l'image photojournalism festival, who died on Monday at the age of 69.

rfi.title: French high schools scramble to work out rules as phone ban takes effect
rfi.description: The new school year starts on Tuesday in France, and with it comes a new rule: mobile phones will no longer be allowed in high schools. The ban came into force a week before the first day of term, leaving schools with little time to work out how to put it into practice.

rfi.title: UN committee presents legal case for broad slavery reparations
rfi.description: Countries are "legally obliged" to provide broad reparations for harms resulting from both direct and indirect involvement in the transatlantic African slave trade, a United Nations committee has said. This comes amid a fresh interpretation of a global accord, published on Monday.

rfi.title: What the SDF’s dissolution means for Syria’s Kurds and neighbouring Turkey
rfi.description: Nearly a week after the Syrian Democratic Forces agreed to dissolve, the consequences are beginning to take shape for Syria's Kurds and neighbouring Turkey. As the former US-backed force is absorbed into the Syrian state, questions remain over what the country's Kurds have secured in return – from language and political rights to protections for women – and what the end of more than a decade of Kurdish-led autonomy means for Turkey's own conflict with Kurdish militants.

rfi.title: Dissident militia in Colombia says kidnapped French Foreign Legion soldier alive
rfi.description: Colombian rebels have claimed responsibility for kidnapping a Colombian soldier serving in the French Foreign Legion, saying he is alive and in good health nearly a month after he was seized in the south-west of the country. However they warned the government against any military intervention.

rfi.title: EU hides disappointment after Iceland's 'No' vote
rfi.description: The EU put a brave face Sunday on Iceland's vote against restarting membership talks, but the outcome was a bitter pill to swallow – robbing Brussels of a hoped-for success story while delighting its eurosceptic critics.

rfi.title: Fils heads into US Open as leader of the French pack as Djokovic bows out
rfi.description: France's top tennis player Arthur Fils will launch his US Open campaign on Monday in the shadow of a shock first round defeat for the fourth seed and four-time champion Novak Djokovic.

rfi.title: PM Lecornu opens political season as French government returns from summer break
rfi.description: French Prime Minister Sébastien Lecornu is bringing his cabinet together on Monday to tackle the increasingly difficult task of drawing up the 2027 budget, with weak growth, rising borrowing costs and the threat of a no-confidence vote narrowing the government’s room for manoeuvre.

rfi.title: French LGBTQ campaigner vows to continue fight after 'despicable' Paris attack
rfi.description: French police officer and LGBTQ rights campaigner Pierre Picavet has vowed to continue fighting discrimination after he was violently attacked outside a bar in Paris this weekend. The suspect of what Paris mayor has described as a "despicable" attack appears in court on Monday.

rfi.title: Macron in Sweden to sign frigate deal, strengthening 'strategic partnership'
rfi.description: Emmanuel Macron will visit Sweden on Monday to sign a €4.3 billion contract for Stockholm's acquisition of four French frigates – a trip that will also provide the French president with an opportunity to discuss broader concerns about European security and NATO cooperation with Sweden's Prime Minister Ulf Kristersson.

rfi.title: Farm workers face a ‘double-edged sword’ of extreme heat and pesticides
rfi.description: As extreme heat makes working outdoors increasingly dangerous, farm workers face another, less visible threat: the pesticides used on the crops around them. Higher temperatures can make these chemicals evaporate faster, increasing workers’ exposure as their bodies are already struggling with the heat.

rfi.title: Zambia's opposition leader charged with treason
rfi.description: Zambia's detained opposition leader Brian Mundubile has been charged with treason, his lawyer said on Sunday, deepening concerns over the government's treatment of political dissent.

rfi.title: Killing of Palestinian children and teens by Israel surges in West Bank
rfi.description: Alia al-Hallaq's son Mohammed was nine when he was killed by an Israeli army bullet last October, but the Palestinian homemaker still speaks of herself as a mother of five, not four.

rfi.title: Women in Zimbabwe push for recognition of 'invisible' domestic labour
rfi.description: In Zimbabwe, women and girls overwhelmingly bear the burden of domestic labour – costing them opportunities outside the home. New policies are being considered to recognise the value of this unpaid work.

rfi.title: Still dancing at 88, Mali’s Mariam Bagayoko keeps tradition alive
rfi.description: At the age of 88, barefoot and cinched into a belt of cowrie shells, renowned singer Mariam Bagayoko still sweeps across the stage with infectious energy, dazzling wide-eyed fans with the rhythms of a bygone Mali.

rfi.title: Guinea-Bissau votes in referendum on giving president more powers
rfi.description: Voters in military-run Guinea-Bissau will cast ballots on Sunday in a referendum that could give the president more powers ahead of a general election meant to restore civilian rule later this year.

france24fr.title: La Cour suprême autorise la construction de la salle de bal de Donald Trump à la Maison Blanche
france24fr.description: La Cour suprême des États-Unis a autorisé lundi Donald Trump à poursuivre les travaux de sa salle de bal à la Maison Blanche, suspendant par cinq voix contre quatre la décision d'appel qui bloquait le chantier, sans toutefois se prononcer sur le fond du recours déposé par le National Trust for Historic Preservation.

france24fr.title: 🔴 Meurtre du rappeur Tupac Shakur : Duane Davis, ancien membre de gang, reconnu coupable
Meurtre du rappeur Tupac Shakur : Duane Davis, ancien membre de gang, reconnu coupable
france24fr.description: Duane "Keffe D" Davis, l'ancien chef des South Side Compton Crips, a été reconnu coupable, lundi par un jury de Las Vegas, d'avoir orchestré le meurtre de Tupac Shakur il y a trente ans. La mort du célèbre rappeur californien était l'un des "cold cases" les plus célèbres des États-Unis.

france24fr.title: L'Union européenne va suspendre ses importations de viande du Brésil
france24fr.description: L'Union européenne va suspendre à partir de jeudi ses importations de volaille et de bœuf brésiliens, ainsi que d'œufs et de miel, faute de garanties suffisantes de Brasília sur le respect des règles sanitaires européennes contre l'usage abusif d'antibiotiques dans l'élevage.

france24fr.title: L'Organisation de coopération de Shanghai : club uni ou divisé ?
france24fr.description: C’est au Kirghizistan que l’Organisation de coopération de Shanghai tient son sommet ce lundi pendant deux jours. Au menu notamment, l’Inde, la Chine, la Russie doivent s’entretenir avec le président iranien afin de discuter d’un soutien suite aux nouvelles sanctions économiques de Washington et au lendemain de nouveaux bombardements. L'occasion de revenir sur les origines et le rôle de l'OCS.

france24fr.title: Retour au calme à Niamey, l'Algérie envoie quatre avions au Niger
france24fr.description: C'est le retour au calme à Niamey. La capitale du Niger a été secouée samedi par une mutinerie déjouée par le régime militaire avec l'appui de son partenaire russe. L'Algérie a envoyé dimanche, dans le cadre de la reprise récente de la coopération avec son voisin, quatre avions de chasse et deux autres avions militaires. Que faut-il comprendre par l'envoi de ces avions? Quels sont les enjeux pour l'Algérie? L'analyse de notre invité invité Akram Kharief, journaliste et directeur de Ménadefense.

france24fr.title: Désastre au Népal : les intox inondent les réseaux sociaux
france24fr.description: 5 jours après la crue dévastatrice qui a déferlé sur le Népal, des images de la catastrophe continuent de se répandre sur les réseaux sociaux. Beaucoup sont générées par l'intelligence artificielle, d'autres présentent des vidéos décontextualisées. Pourquoi certains internautes surenchérissent, alors que les images réelles sont déjà très impressionnantes ? Explications avec Jules BOITEAU dans Info Intox.

france24fr.title: 🔴 L'ancien Premier ministre Édouard Balladur est mort à l'âge de 97 ans
Mort de l'ancien Premier ministre Édouard Balladur à 97 ans
france24fr.description: Édouard Balladur, Premier ministre entre 1993 et 1995, est mort lundi à 97 ans. Ancien proche de Jacques Chirac, il était devenu son rival lors de la campagne présidentielle de 1995. Son échec au premier tour avait mis fin à ses ambitions nationales.

france24fr.title: Crise au Népal : onde de choc régionale ?
france24fr.description: Au Népal, le bilan des victimes est revu à la hausse chaque jour. Des identifications sont toujours en cours. "Une catastrophe naturelle déchirante",  a jugé le Premier Ministre du Népal Balendra Shah. Plusieurs questions ce soir dans le débat : Comment le Népal gère-t-il les secours ? Quel rôle jouent l'Inde et la Chine ? Quid des Etats-Unis et de l'Europe ? La catastrophe climatique d'aujourd'hui peut-elle dégénérer en une catastrophe humanitaire ? Doit-on s'attendre à une déstabilisation de l

france24fr.title: Niger : le calme revient à Niamey après la mutinerie
france24fr.description: 🇳🇪 Au Niger, le calme est de retour à Niamey, après une nuit de vendredi à samedi marquée par une mutinerie déjouée par le régime militaire. Avec l’appui de ses alliés russes, les paramilitaires d’Africa Corps ont effectué une tournée dans la capitale. Retour en images avec Gaëlle Fonseca.

france24fr.title: RD Congo : l'opposition rejette les consultations annoncées par Tshisekedi
france24fr.description: 🇨🇩 En RDC, le projet de dialogue national de Félix Tshisekedi divise déjà. L’opposition, réunie au sein de la coalition C64 et les partisans de Joseph Kabila, rejette les consultations annoncées. La majorité présidentielle, elle, défend le processus.

france24fr.title: Cameroun : Les migrants expulsés des États-Unis dénoncent leurs conditions
france24fr.description: 🇨🇲 🇺🇸 Le Cameroun fait partie des pays qui auraient conclu un accord secret avec les États-Unis pour accueillir des personnes expulsées. Alors que ces personnes vivent souvent dans des conditions précaires et risquent de subir des persécutions similaires à celles de leur pays d’origine.

france24fr.title: Crue dans le Grand Canyon: le rôle du changement climatique
france24fr.description: Une crue soudaine dans le Grand Canyon a fait au moins 1 mort et 15 disparus. La rivière qui coule dans la Bright Angel Creek a vu son débit multiplié par 20 en un temps très court. Sur le sol aride, donc imperméable, de la zone et à la faveur de pentes très raides, un mur d'eau a fondu sur les randonneurs. Le changement climatique joue un rôle dans l'amplification des averses. Et la rapidité de ces modifications du système climatique rend plus difficile la prévision de ces événements extrêmes.

france24fr.title: Venezuela : Alejandro Betancourt, le sulfureux magnat du pétrole sur lequel Trump veut miser
france24fr.description: En annonçant vendredi avoir conclu un accord avec le Venezuela pour obtenir “65 milliards de barils” de pétrole, Donald Trump avait précisé que Washington travaillerait avec un intermédiaire. Il s’agit d’Alejandro Betancourt, un homme d’affaires controversé qui a fait fortune grâce au chavisme.

france24fr.title: Massachusetts : une nouvelle loi autorise-t-elle l’avortement "jusqu’à l’accouchement" ?
france24fr.description: Depuis l’adoption d’une nouvelle loi sur l’avortement au Massachusetts, plusieurs publications virales sur les réseaux sociaux affirment que l’État autoriserait désormais les interruptions de grossesse jusqu’au jour de la naissance. Qu’en est-il vraiment ?

france24fr.title: The Cure, Interpol, et interdiction de fumer : les temps forts de Rock en Seine
france24fr.description: Sur les cinq jours du festival de Rock en Seine, 175 000 personnes ont répondu présentes malgré les aléas de la météo. Le dernier festival de musique de l'été a fait le plein aux portes de Paris. Retour sur les meilleurs moments.

phys-org.title: Cover crops could ease the shift from perennial seed to annual crops
phys-org.description: Transitioning an aging perennial forage seed stand into annual cropping can be difficult, particularly when the original crop persists or weeds establish after termination. Preliminary Canadian research suggests cover crops could help by suppressing regrowth and weeds, retaining biomass and cycling nutrients.

phys-org.title: Drones take farming to new heights
phys-org.description: High above the fields of the Morven Sustainability Lab, drones equipped with heat and light sensors are changing what it means to farm smarter. This month, researchers and students from the University of Virginia, NASA and the University at Buffalo tested drone technology by flying more than 100 feet (30 meters) above crops to measure plant health at UVA's 2,900-acre (1,170-hectare) research facility.

phys-org.title: Australia's reefs follow trend of global coral cover decline
phys-org.description: Australia's coral reefs are in relatively good condition compared with coral reefs globally, although coral cover on Australian reefs has declined over the past 40 years—reflecting the global trend, a major new report has found.

phys-org.title: Important role of plastid ion channels in plant stress response identified
phys-org.description: When plants are attacked by herbivores or pathogens, they must respond rapidly while also preparing for potential future attacks. Calcium, a cellular second messenger, and the plant hormone jasmonic acid play important roles in this response. Within seconds of an injury, the plant generates calcium waves that relay information about the attack. phys-org.title: Even small amounts of ocean plastic can affect petrel chicks
phys-org.description: Ocean plastic pollution is accidentally on the menu for southern giant petrel chicks. Even small nibbles of it may affect their physiology during development, according to a study from the University of California, Davis, and Argentina's National Research Council (CONICET).

phys-org.title: Sliding sugars offer simpler, smarter route to precision liver-targeted therapies
phys-org.description: Targeted drug delivery directly to the liver has unlocked major breakthroughs across medicine, but constructing the chemical key to enter liver cells remains complex and costly. Today, researchers at Kumamoto University, in collaboration with the National University of Singapore, have unveiled a nature-inspired solution that bypasses synthetic bottlenecks by giving single sugar molecules room to move. Their findings are published in the journal Advanced Science.

phys-org.description: Communication between cells in plants, animals and humans takes place via specialized connecting structures. An international team led by biologists from Heinrich Heine University Düsseldorf (HHU) and involving the University of Tübingen has now discovered that the regulation of very similar structures was already present in multicellular bacteria, implying that it must have originated much earlier in the course of evolution. In their paper published in The EMBO Journal, the researchers describe

phys-org.title: AI chatbot use for emotional support tied to loneliness in students
phys-org.description: Young people leaning on AI chatbots for emotional support or personal advice are significantly more likely to struggle with serious emotional problems, feel isolated and doubt that they truly matter to others, a new uOttawa study warns.

phys-org.title: Role of ethics education in accounting fraud prevention
phys-org.description: Two SUNY Polytechnic Institute (SUNY Poly) College of Business faculty members are exploring how integrating ethics and values throughout accounting and business education can better prepare students to recognize and prevent fraud in the workplace.

phys-org.description: Biologists and linguists alike have long puzzled over the universal human tendency to see and name colors as a combination of four "pure" hues—red, yellow, green and blue.

phys-org.title: Faint far-infrared radiation drives a correlated insulator-to-metal transition in magic-angle graphene
phys-org.description: One of the central ideas in modern physics is the phase transition—a sudden transformation of the state of a material. We encounter phase transitions throughout everyday life: water freezes into ice, wax melts in the warmth of a flame, and water vapor condenses into droplets on a cold window. In these familiar examples, the atoms themselves rearrange into a new structure, giving the material entirely different properties.

phys-org.title: A single fix reverses the case for rolling back vehicle emissions standards
phys-org.description: Two administrations, the Biden administration and the second Trump administration, reached opposite conclusions about whether vehicle emissions standards should be rolled back. These conclusions came from different assumptions, including whether avoiding air pollution has value to society and the degree to which car buyers value future fuel savings from getting a more efficient vehicle. phys-org.title: Q&A: What dinosaur teeth reveal about diet and evolution
phys-org.description: What did dinosaurs eat? Teeth provide important clues to understanding the ecology of dinosaurs, which became extinct approximately 66 million years ago. Their shape, structure and patterns of wear can help scientists reconstruct how these animals obtained and processed their food.

phys-org.title: Femtosecond nano-imaging reveals ultrafast optical control of phonon polaritons
phys-org.description: A collaborative research team has successfully visualized in real space the ultrafast optical modulation of hyperbolic phonon polaritons (HPhPs)  in a van der Waals heterostructure composed of hBN and WS2. The research is published in the journal Nano Letters, and was led by Kazuki Kamada of the Institute for Molecular Science (IMS) and Osaka Metropolitan University, along with Dr. Jun Nishida, assistant professor at IMS, and Takashi Kumagai, associate professor at IMS.

phys-org.title: Managing chronic conditions together may be key to longer lifespan, canine study finds
phys-org.description: As dogs age, many develop more than one chronic health condition. New research from Texas A&M College of Veterinary Medicine and Biomedical Sciences (VMBS) shows those conditions can dramatically shorten a dog's lifespan, highlighting the importance of managing multiple diseases together rather than individually.

This is primarily due to their active geology, including Io being the most volcanically active planetary body in the solar system and Europa having a vast subsurface liquid-water ocean beneath its icy crust. phys-org.title: Organic crystal reveals how Joule heating stabilizes resistive switching

undark.title: Book Review: Our Conflicted Relationship with the Sun
undark.description: Despite dermatological guidelines that decree sunlight a harmful carcinogen, Rowan Jacobsen argues in “In Defense of Sunlight” that the sun helps our skin produce many compounds vital to our health. How did science miss these benefits? The answer, he says, lies in our inability to do things in moderation.

undark.title: The New Student Visa Policy Doesn’t Add Up
undark.description: In July, the Department of Homeland Security issued new rules that would make it harder for international students to complete their studies in the U.S. The policy threatens to be disruptive for students — particularly doctoral candidates — and self-defeating for the country.

undark.title: Book Review: How Wildlife Is Returning to the East
undark.description: In “The Beasts of the East,” journalist Andrew Moore charts the natural history of the East and the people who have dedicated their careers to restoring several long lost species to what remains of their original habitats.

undark.title: Book Review: The Case for the AI-Powered Global Brain
undark.description: In “The God Test,” Robert Wright considers a future in which human consciousness becomes infused with AI. “We have to think seriously about a future in which there is something that increasingly resembles a global brain, and its neurons increasingly consist not just of human brains but of AIs,” he writes.

undark.title: Interview: How Tragedy Changed the FDA
undark.description: As an FDA advisory committee prepares to weigh whether specialized pharmacies should be allowed to dispense seven unapproved peptides, Mikkael A. Sekeres, a scientist and former adviser, discusses the history and nuances of FDA oversight, including its process for screening advisory committee members for conflicts of interest.

undark.title: Will AI Fix Prior Authorization — or Make It Worse?
undark.description: The Trump administration is currently piloting a program in six states that expands Medicare prior authorizations using AI tools in an effort to reduce unnecessary medical spending. But it remains to be seen whether this new approach, which the administration has called “broken” in the private sector, will be effective without causing dangerous delays for Medicare recipients.

undark.title: Biologists Should Articulate Their Position on AI
undark.description: Last month, mathematics researchers released the Leiden Declaration, a treatise on how to handle the challenges that artificial intelligence poses to their field. C. Brandon Ogbunu argues that biologists should learn from the mathematics community and work on their own version.

undark.title: Review: What Animals Can Teach Humans About Caregiving
undark.description: From seahorses and birds to beetles and killer whales, journalist Elizabeth Preston finds a lot of common ground  between human and animal parenting in “The Creatures’ Guide to Caring,” a sweeping survey of the evolution of caregiving and the dizzying array of survival strategies in the animal kingdom.

undark.title: The MAHA Movement’s Worrisome Embrace of Ibogaine
undark.description: The MAHA movement has been promoting the plant-based substance ibogaine as a remedy for opioid addiction, despite the lack of clinical trials on its safety and efficacy. One physician who practices addiction medicine discusses the risks of ibogaine and argues for the need to support proven treatments.

undark.title: Advocacy Groups Express Mixed Views on Embryo Editing
undark.description: At least two new start-up companies, Preventive and Origin Genomics, say they are developing strategies that combine gene editing with in vitro fertilization to correct disease-causing mutations. Advocacy groups for people living with these genetic disorders have been quiet on the developments.

proj-syn.title: Are The Walls Closing in on Bessent?
proj-syn.description: Far from suggesting financial Armageddon, US Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent’s futile efforts to keep a lid on Treasury yields suggest that, once again, the dollar is America’s currency, but everyone else’s problem. But while investors have few alternatives, the bond-salesman-in-chief cannot be complacent.

proj-syn.title: AI Is Reviving Chinese Marxist Economics
proj-syn.description: As recently as two years ago, most Chinese economists paid only lip service to Marxism and assigned Western textbooks to their students. The advent of AI has changed that, because the technology—open source and available to the smallest manufacturer for a pittance—promises to avoid the “rent trap” common to capitalist economies.

proj-syn.title: Gen Z Is Transforming South Asia
proj-syn.description: Facing diminished economic prospects, many young people see not flawed institutions in need of gradual reform, but predatory systems robbing them of their future. Across South Asia, this sense has animated powerful protest movements, some of which could shape their countries' political trajectories for decades to come.

proj-syn.title: How Britain Can Help Build a Fairer Global Economy
proj-syn.description: With the United Kingdom poised to preside over both the G20 and the G7, Prime Minister Andy Burnham has a unique opportunity to usher in a new internationalism grounded not in military posturing, but in the pursuit of a fairer global economy. But he must abandon his predecessor’s defensive approach.

proj-syn.title: Technocracy Can’t Fix Europe
proj-syn.description: A new private initiative bringing together the crème de la crème of European business, financial, economic, and tech elites could well prove useful in kick-starting European growth and innovation. But first, it must recognize that the problem it hopes to solve is fundamentally political.

proj-syn.title: The Fed and the Treasury Are in Denial
proj-syn.description: For most of the postwar era, the United States has enjoyed a privileged position as an issuer of both sovereign debt and US dollars that always found takers. But the US may no longer be able to rely on stable demand for its debt or its currency, forcing policymakers to face the truth about how financial markets are made.

proj-syn.title: To End Global Hunger, Invest in Rural Communities
proj-syn.description: Even as hunger declines around the world, food insecurity remains prevalent in rural communities. Restoring soil health, expanding access to new technologies, strengthening land rights, and upgrading public infrastructure are essential to boost agricultural productivity and protect rural livelihoods.

proj-syn.title: The Sanctions Illusion
proj-syn.description: Those who defend sweeping financial sanctions against countries like Russia and Iran often claim that popular suffering is a defensible means of pressuring the target government. But while such measures certainly inflict widespread suffering on civilian populations, this rarely translates into political change.

proj-syn.title: Is Monetarism Making a Comeback?
proj-syn.description: After decades on the margins of mainstream economic thinking, monetarism is beginning to re-enter the debate, most notably at the Federal Reserve. To regain credibility, however, monetarists must learn from past mistakes and adapt to the monetary and financial realities of the 21st century.

proj-syn.title: China’s Super-Dam Is Becoming an Upstream Water Bomb
proj-syn.description: The latest evidence suggests that the Chinese scientific establishment understands the dangers of a planned Himalayan dam—the world's largest—more clearly than its political leadership is willing to acknowledge. With the livelihoods of two billion people at stake, the international community needs to weigh in.

proj-syn.title: Europe and the War in Ukraine
proj-syn.description: If Europe remains a mere collection of small states and middle powers, the current period of profound geopolitical and historical change will also mark the end of its role on the world stage. With no end in sight for Russia's war in Ukraine, Europeans must come to grips with reality.

proj-syn.title: Europe Must Stand with Canada Against Trump
proj-syn.description: Rather than keeping their heads down as US President Donald Trump wages another trade war with Canada, European leaders must recognize that they could be next. Like Canada, the European Union is a middle power whose future prosperity and security will depend on solidarity with economic peers.

proj-syn.title: Is China Really a Champion of the Global South?
proj-syn.description: The United States is an overextended hegemon, and its decline will continue slowly, as other powers like China assume more global responsibilities. Against this backdrop, China’s efforts to lead the Global South are more about consolidating its power in the current international system than creating a new one that benefits all.

proj-syn.title: The Economist’s Embarrassing Proxy War Over AI Policy
proj-syn.description: The disagreements between the Nobel laureate economist Daron Acemoglu and his opponents are consequential—and so are the opponents. But rather than engage in good faith with Acemoglu's arguments, the venerable British news magazine recently stooped to bibulous calumny by unnamed critics of his work.

proj-syn.title: Democracies Must Get Serious About Industrial Policy
proj-syn.description: For decades, Western governments have ceded the strategic direction of their economies to the market. To dominate the industries of the future, they must learn from their own history and rebuild the institutions, expertise, and discipline that effective industrial policy demands.

proj-syn.title: In the AI Gold Rush, the Cloud Wins
proj-syn.description: Even if the AI investment boom turns out to have been a bubble, the Big Tech companies that have cornered the cloud infrastructure market will emerge as strong as ever, or even stronger. That is why Amazon, Microsoft, and Google are in a league of their own, even compared to other giants like Meta and Nvidia.
